verified.exploit_entry_point: Every security case drives a public entry point of the package: customAlphabet() / customRandom() imported from the package root (the Node export condition) and the browser export condition module, nanoid() and customAlphabet() from the documented non-secure module, and the bundled command-line tool. Each call runs in its own process with a hard 4 s timeout; a call that does not return is the failure. Values are literals in the case tables, never computed with the product.
sites: index.js:53-56 (the custom generator closure: effective size and creation-time progress)
index.browser.js:36-39 (the bundler / react-native copy of the same decisions)
index.browser.js:42-45 (the same copy's exit test, which a zero default reaches after one character)
non-secure/index.js:28-29 (the non-secure plain ID call countdown)
bin/nanoid.js:35-38 (numeric conversion and positivity test of the size argument)
routes: T1: zero and negative effective sizes through the custom generator closure
T2: the same input through the bundler / react-native export condition
T3: negative effective sizes through the non-secure custom generator
T4: negative sizes, including numeric text, through the non-secure plain ID call
T5: non-numeric and unbounded sizes through the custom generator closure
T6: an alphabet with no symbols in both generator copies
T7: a non-positive creation default combined with an explicit positive call size
T8 (coupled, functional): omitted sizes, numeric strings, fractional sizes, a one-symbol alphabet, a caller-supplied byte source and the command-line alphabet-only invocation
T9: an overflowing numeric size literal through the bundled command-line tool
T10: non-numeric and unbounded sizes through the bundler / react-native copy
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own test files for the affected area (test/index.test.js, test/non-secure.test.js, test/bin.test.js: 47 cases) run from pristine copies staged at grade time on the pinned tree, the reference fix and every check patch; the hidden functional suite adds 27 cases.

traps.shape: a zero or negative effective size reaching the custom generator creation; the closure's exit test uses the call size, which for a zero creation default is also the size that never advances the loop
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is one zero size, so a one-line non-positive test in the Node closure looks complete
traps.realistic_because: the advisory's own route at the pinned commit (published fix cb3626d touches this closure)

traps.shape: the bundler / react-native copy of the same generator has its own creation-time step arithmetic and its own closure; a zero default there returns one character instead of blocking, so a Node-side reproduction looks complete without it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the module is selected only by the browser / react-native export condition (package.json:35, 36, 42, 45), so a Node reproduction of the reported blocking call never reaches it
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the later published fix f9d13f1 adds the same decision to this copy

traps.shape: the documented non-secure implementation's custom generator counts down a 32-bit integer; a negative effective size makes the countdown run without bound
traps.reason_to_dismiss: nanoid/non-secure is documented as the explicitly non-secure alternative and its loop is a countdown, not a while(true); size 0 already returns an empty ID there
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; neither published fix commit touches this module

traps.shape: the plain non-secure ID call repeats the same countdown, so a negative size (including one written as numeric text) blocks there as well
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory names custom generators; the plain non-secure ID call is a different entry point, and the secure implementation converts its size with a 32-bit coercion that yields an empty ID rather than looping
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; untouched by the published fix commits

traps.shape: the same closure's exit test compares against the caller's size, so a non-numeric or unbounded size makes that comparison false forever; a non-positive test misses these values
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a zero or negative integer is not the same input as a value that is not a number or is not finite, and the obvious non-positive test does not fire on them
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published final behaviour (size <= 0) leaves these values looping

traps.shape: progress is decided when the generator is created: an alphabet with no symbols derives a creation-time quantity that cannot advance the loop, in the Node copy and, for a different arithmetic reason, in the bundler copy
traps.reason_to_dismiss: alphabet validity is presented as the caller's precondition, and an empty alphabet is not a size at all, so the reported input shape never reaches it
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; neither published fix commit touches creation-time progress

traps.shape: the creation-time default size drives the loop quantity while the exit test uses the call size, so a non-positive creation default blocks even when the call passes a valid positive size
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported case is a zero size with no argument; an explicit positive call size looks like a valid call, and the exit test compares that positive size, so the creation-time quantity is never inspected
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix only tests the call size

traps.shape: the effective size is produced by the closure default from the creation-time default; a guard written on the raw argument, at the creation boundary, or with a type test either misses the defaulted call or turns every defaulted call into an empty ID
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the defaulted call works today, so nothing looks wrong; the coupling only shows when a fix is placed on the raw argument or at the creation boundary
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: T8 is the coupled must-keep value of the size decision; an over-broad or boundary-placed fix is proved wrong by checks/functional_overbroad.patch (functional_fail) and by the functional cases above
traps.realistic_because: the project's own tests pin these values (test/index.test.js:92-95, 124-126, 47-49, 129-136) and the command-line tool relies on the creation-time default

traps.shape: the bundled command-line tool converts its size argument with a numeric conversion that accepts an overflowing numeric literal as a positive value, then hands it to a custom generator; the tool's own positive/NaN test passes it through
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the command-line tool already rejects non-numeric and non-positive sizes, and an overflowing numeric literal is a numeric-syntax curiosity that passes the positivity test
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: T9 uses the same size decision as T1/T5 and is proved by the predicate breadth in checks/miss_c1_node_size.patch together with the independent checks/crash_refusal.patch (the first published fix)
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fixes never touch the command-line tool

traps.shape: the bundler copy's exit test has the same blind spot for non-numeric and unbounded sizes; its creation-time arithmetic also differs enough that the zero case terminates there, which hides the missing decision
traps.reason_to_dismiss: once the Node copy is fixed and reproduced, the bundler copy looks handled; its zero default terminating makes a Node-derived test of the size decision look complete
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published final fix (size <= 0) leaves these values looping in this copy
